findings.title: Caller-authored profile fields can manufacture an analogy
attack_path: A caller attaches misleading structured features to an existing task.
Exact-scope retrieval computes a high deterministic score.
A downstream consumer could over-trust the historical analogy.
evidence: Profile evidence is required but not independently authenticated.
Every result is analogy-only and execution_authority is false.
findings.recommendation: Require current validation and explicit authorization before reusing a historical plan, tool, or artifact.

findings.title: Structured tokens remain non-executable data
attack_path: A caller supplies crafted intent, artifact, tool, or environment tokens.
The strict normalized-token parser rejects whitespace and control syntax.
Retained values are compared as data and no command, prompt, or tool is invoked.
evidence: Tokens use a bounded normalized grammar and secret scanning.
The engine never reads task objectives or executes returned tool names.
findings.recommendation: Keep downstream rendering escaped and retain the closed capability vocabulary.

findings.title: Exact scope and Safe Mode constrain profile use
attack_path: A caller attempts a profile write during containment or seeks another scope's history.
The embedded mutation guard blocks the write and SQL requires the target's exact scope.
No cross-scope analogy or profile mutation succeeds.
evidence: Direct engine Safe Mode behavior is tested.
Similarity SQL filters terminal tasks by exact target scope.
findings.recommendation: Preserve both guards if interfaces change.

findings.title: Historical scans and outputs are bounded and content minimized
attack_path: A scope accumulates many profiled tasks.
The engine reads at most 501 candidates and fails closed above 500.
Results omit objectives and traces and return at most 50 analogies.
evidence: Candidate and output bounds are enforced and tested.
Only explicit profile metadata and bounded task outcome fields are returned.
findings.recommendation: Benchmark and add pagination before increasing bounds.

limitations: Profile provenance is caller asserted rather than authenticated.
The fixed weights are transparent but not calibrated.
Structural similarity is not evidence of causal transfer or future success.
No embeddings, model calls, network, filesystem, shell, tool execution, or automatic solution reuse occurs.
